back_translation: On the first day of the third month, in the eleventh year, the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his multitude: To whom can you be compared in your greatness?
Behold, Assyria was a cedar in Lebanon, with beautiful branches that gave shade to the forest, towering high, its top among the thick clouds.
The waters nourished it and made it grow; the deep made it tall, sending its rivers around the place where it was planted and its channels to all the trees of the field.
Therefore it towered higher than all the trees of the field; its branches multiplied and its boughs grew long because of the abundant waters as it spread them out.
All the birds of the air nested in its branches, all the beasts of the field gave birth beneath its boughs, and all the great nations lived in its shade.
It was beautiful in its greatness, in the length of its branches, for its roots reached down to abundant waters.
The cedars in the garden of God could not rival it; the cypresses could not compare with its branches, nor the plane trees with its boughs. No tree in the garden of God could compare with its beauty.
I made it beautiful with its many branches, so that all the trees of Eden that were in the garden of God envied it.
Therefore the Lord GOD says this: Because it towered high and set its top among the thick clouds, and its heart grew proud because of its height,
I gave it into the hand of the mighty one of the nations, for him to deal with it according to its wickedness. I have driven it out.

Foreigners, the most ruthless of nations, cut it down and left it. Its branches fell on the mountains and in all the valleys; its boughs lay broken in all the ravines of the land; and all the peoples of the earth went away from its shade and abandoned it.
All the birds of the air settled on its fallen trunk, and all the beasts of the field were among its boughs.

This was so that no trees by the waters would grow tall in their height or set their tops among the thick clouds, and that no well-watered trees would stand up to them in their height; for they were all consigned to death, to the world below, among the sons of men, with those who go down to the Pit.

The Lord GOD says this: On the day it went down to Sheol, I caused mourning. I covered the deep over it, held back its rivers, and the abundant waters were restrained. I made Lebanon mourn for it, and all the trees of the field fainted because of it.

I made the nations quake at the sound of its downfall when I cast it down to Sheol with those who go down to the Pit. Then all the trees of Eden, the choicest and best of Lebanon, all the well-watered trees, were comforted in the world below.
They too went down with it to Sheol, to those slain by the sword—its allies who had lived in its shade among the nations.

To which of the trees of Eden can you be compared in glory and greatness? Yet you will be brought down with the trees of Eden to the world below; you will lie among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord GOD.”
